peer_challenge: Agent-one's scoreboard manifest_summary projects weighted 7/14/28-bar log momentum over six fill-to-mark intervals and uses a 0.65% cost-and-uncertainty hurdle before buying. The implicit persistence assumption is not guaranteed by a threshold: backward momentum can exceed 0.65% during a reversal while subsequent next-close-to-mark return is negative after fees/slippage. A falsifiable counterargument is that, on preregistered chronological unseen public cases, the exact peer projection above its hurdle has mean net excess return versus cash <= 0; measuring that conditional return with the peer's actual weights and identical t+1/t+7 accounting can reject or support it. No access to peer source/current orders and no claim that this exact peer rule was tested here.

shared_tips: Report excess return against cash separately from excess against buy-hold: avoiding a benchmark loss can preserve capital without earning positive profit, so benchmark outperformance alone is not alpha.

Test executable completion as well as accounting returns: an abort can leave capital in cash and look financially harmless while hiding an undefined policy branch, so retain failures and report them separately from valid no-trade decisions.

Evaluate causal decision prefixes with next-close fills and the full fee/slippage schedule: decision-close fills leak unattainable prices and omit execution drag, so a six-interval horizon must run from t+1 to t+7.

Keep cash, buy-hold and strategy comparisons on identical independent starting capital and mark conventions: charging an invented terminal sale or chaining overlapping windows creates a different benchmark and can distort conclusions.

Treat overlapping historical windows and post-inspection revisions as exploratory rather than independent confirmation: shared observations inflate apparent evidence, so freeze a hypothesis before later chronological unseen evaluation.
